coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 45–55 min Z2 (140–150 bpm), rolling terrain, no hard efforts. Your resting HR is 7.5 bpm above your 30-day average and recovery score sits at 46/100—both signals of incomplete recovery. You've run 18.2 miles this week already (11.82 + 12.04 + 6.41), which is solid volume for taper, but your last three efforts averaged 128 bpm, indicating sustained aerobic work without easy days in between. Today is active recovery: keep it conversational, sub-threshold, and treat it as a mobility run. The Julian Alps terrain will punish accumulated fatigue far more than it will punish a slow Sunday.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Eat carbs + protein within 30 min of finishing: 40–50g carbs (rice, oats, fruit) + 15–20g protein (yogurt, eggs, chicken). Your sleep efficiency dipped to 70% last night despite 8.3 hours—possible sign of glycogen depletion or elevated cortisol. During taper, prioritize carb loading to top off stores (aim 6–8g/kg bodyweight daily). If you've been traveling for work, that's your culprit for the elevated RHR; front-load breakfast and lunch with dense carbs tomorrow through race week to offset travel stress and build glycogen resilience.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep 8–9 hours tonight, prioritize cool/dark conditions, and avoid screens 60 min before bed. Your 70% sleep efficiency is below your 30-day average (implied closer to 75–80%), which suggests sleep *quality* is eroding even if quantity looks okay—likely stress, jet lag, or insufficient pre-sleep wind-down. Hit 9 hours if possible; you're 26 days out and need RHR back below 66. Consider a 10–15 min easy walk or foam roll instead of stretching if you feel stiff; avoid any massage or aggressive trigger work that spikes inflammation.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You've logged solid volume through peak phase and are now in the critical taper window—trust the work, don't panic. Your last three runs (11.82, 12.04, 6.41 mi) show you're handling vert and aerobic load, which are exactly what a 2,500m alpine 50K demands. The elevated RHR and moderate recovery score are *normal* at this point; they'll drop as volume dwindles and sleep solidifies over the next 2–3 days. Kranjska Gora rewards patience and power on the descents—focus on sleep and easy efforts now, not on fitting in extra work.
